mentions.name: WishKeeper
mentions.description: This webapp lets users create wish lists and share them with family and friends. Its key feature is a claim system: when someone decides to buy an item, they claim it so other shoppers know it's taken, while the list owner never sees who claimed what or even that it was claimed, keeping the surprise intact. It also supports splitting big purchases so multiple people can chip in toward expensive items, letting those on tight budgets contribute without pressuring list owners to add small items. The app is deliberately simple—no social features, feeds, or ads—just lists with items, links, prices, and notes. It is free to use with no credit card required.
mentions.problem: Group gift coordination is awkward: shoppers duplicate purchases or feel obligated to buy small items just so everyone can contribute, and seeing that a gift was claimed spoils the surprise for the list owner.
mentions.audience: Families and friends who share wish lists for birthdays and holidays, including family members with tight budgets who want to chip in on bigger gifts.
mentions.source_excerpt:
I'm working on WishKeeper https://wishkeeper.io.

It's a webapp that lets you create wish lists and share them with family and friends. The key feature is the claim system: when someone decides to buy you an item, they can claim it so others know it's taken, but you never see who claimed what or even that it was claimed at all. The surprise stays intact.
